source.title: Contrastive Multi-modal Training with Electrocardiography and Natural Language Echocardiography Reports for Zero-shot Prediction of Structural Heart Disease
source.authors: Wing-Cheuk Wong; C. Liu; P. Elias; J. Hughes; Christopher H. Leung; X.-Y. Qian; H.-L. Li; Y.-M. Lau; C.-F. Tao; A. Choo; Conklin Yung; C. Fong; Wooyeop Choi; C.-K.-A. Cheng; L.-L. Cheng; Lkw Lau; R. Relwani; J. Qin; L. Yu; H. Lui; H.-O. A. C. Chiu; H.-F. Tse; Clara Siu; R. Arcucci; J. W. Ho; C.-K. Wong

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some equations are garbled in the text extraction, but the reported scaling results and tables are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies training-set size and reports downstream AUROC for an ECG model, a different modality and outcome from language-model pretraining loss. This bears on V6, but does not test the original power-law loss claims.
record.gate_note: The relevant result is AUROC across five training-set sizes for two ECG encoders, with and without ECG–ECG text pretraining (Table 3). The study does not measure held-out cross-entropy, vary parameter count or training compute, fit power laws, or test extrapolation. Architecture, prompt, pretraining, and text-processing comparisons that do not measure the scaling behavior named in a claim version are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: This is a clinical ECG–ECHO-report CLIP study. Its only scaling result (Table 3, Figure 4A) is zero-shot AUROC of the ECG encoders (1D-ResNet18, ViT-Tiny) at 20–100% of a 40,500-pair fine-tuning set. That is a 5× range, under one order of magnitude, with no power-law fit, no loss, no parameter or compute variation and no extrapolation. The system is a small ECG signal encoder aligned to a frozen-mostly MedCPT text encoder, not a language model, so the rows do not measure what V6 (downstream predictability of language-model scale) names. V5 would need the power-law form to be tested in another modality, and it is not. Kaplan et al. is cited only to say accuracy improves with more data. The data-size ablation is a related finding and is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say ResNet18 models, with and without ECG–ECG text pretraining, improve AUROC steadily with data, without a plateau. They report a 9% gain from 20% to 100% with pretraining, and read this as headroom for larger ECG–ECHO foundation models. They also find ResNet18 beats ViT-Tiny by about 6–7% AUROC on full data, which they attribute to convolutions capturing local ECG features. Their main conclusion is about zero-shot SHD detection, not scaling.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales ECG training-data size and measures downstream AUROC; it does not use language-model held-out cross-entropy or fit a scaling law.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported AUROC trend differs by ECG encoder and by whether ECG–ECG text pretraining is used; training-set size also varies.

fits_no_version.finding: In an ECG–ECHO-text CLIP model, zero-shot AUROC rises monotonically with fine-tuning data (20%→100%) for ResNet18 with pretraining (59.9→68.9) and without it (49.4→63.6), and for ViT-Tiny with pretraining (51.7→62.7). ViT-Tiny without pretraining stays flat (52.8→52.2). No fits or uncertainty are reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream performance of non-language multimodal (ECG–text) encoders improves with fine-tuning data size, conditional on encoder architecture and pretraining.

record.peer_reviewed: medRxiv preprint; not certified by peer review
record.problems: The scaling results concern downstream AUROC in an ECG model, not language-model loss. The study reports no power-law fits or extrapolation tests, and Table 3 gives no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: None of the relevant training-set-size results in Table 3 were left out.

untested.parts: Language-model pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
Extrapolation of fitted laws to larger runs.
Shape effects at fixed parameter count. The ResNet18 vs ViT-Tiny comparison is not at matched size and does not measure loss.
No power-law form is fitted or tested for the ECG modality or for fine-tuning data size.
There is no language-model downstream scaling. The ECG encoder data-size trend spans 5× with no predictive fit.
No exponents are fitted, so fit-dependence is not addressed.

record.verdict_notes: The reader labelled this as a T3 test of V6 with supports/limits_scope labels. That is not justified: the system is not a language model, and the 5× data-size ablation has no fit or predictive test. No verdicts are given. The ViT-Tiny no-pretraining series is flat, not reversed.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether power laws fitted on small runs predict substantially larger runs.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture details on language-model loss at fixed parameter count.
Whether the same power-law form holds in other modalities or training regimes; the study does not fit or test a power-law form.
The study reports downstream AUROC across ECG training-data sizes, but does not test language models, pretraining-loss predictability, or predictive fits from smaller runs.
Dependence of language-model scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocation on fitting choices or setup.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ResNet18 with and without ECG–ECG text pretraining, and ViT-Tiny with pretraining
reader_labels.reason: AUROC increases at every larger training-set size relative to the 20% reference in these series (rows r1–r5, r6–r10, r11–r15).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: AUROC does not rise steadily with training-set size: it falls at 40%, briefly exceeds the reference at 60%, then remains below the reference at 80% and 100% (rows r16–r20).
